overall: Tomorrow (Wednesday, June 25) is expected to be sunny and warm in Atlanta with light southeast winds of 0-5 mph and no precipitation chance. It will be a classic early summer day with temperatures comfortably climbing into the upper 80s. The active NWS flood warnings are limited to the Satilla River basin in far southeastern Georgia (Pierce, Ware, and Brantley Counties) and are not relevant to the Atlanta area.
forecast_obs_notes: Model consensus is reasonably tight with most sources clustering in the 86-90°F range: ECMWF at ~88.1°F, HRRR at ~89.7°F, NBM at ~86.4°F, and Weather.com at ~87.5°F all broadly agree. GFS is a notable cold outlier at ~77.7°F, pulling the ensemble mean slightly lower, but the majority of guidance dismisses this lower solution.
max_temp_prediction: The full ensemble model projects a TMAX of 87.0°F, well-supported by the NWS official forecast of 86°F and the multi-model consensus in the 86-90°F band. Sunny skies, light winds, and a warm airmass are the primary drivers. Confidence is moderate — the even-bucket tier is classified as Tier 2 (Good confidence, ~52% expected accuracy) with top probability mass in the 88-91°F zone, but the odd-bucket set shows poor signal agreement, so some spread around the point estimate is warranted.
